newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm in thin trade as holiday begins.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm in thin trade as holiday begins.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed in extremely thin morning trade as the market entered a a 6-1/2-day holiday at midday on Thurday, brokers said.
The stock market will reopen on April 24.
The IMKB National-100 closed nine points, or 0.59 percent higher at 1,532 after moving between 1,516 and 1,533. Morning volume shrank to 5.66 trillion lira from Wednesday's 8.44 trillion.

"The market lacked direction ahead of the holiday and because of uneasiness caused by the forthcoming National Security Council (MGK) meeting. I do not expect much activity after the holiday," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.

The market is unnerved by the MGK meeting scheduled for April 26 following a rift which emerged between the coalition's Islamist and conservative wings after the secularist military demanded measures against rising Islamist activism in the February 28 MGK meeting.
"There may be a rise if political tension eases after the holiday and if trade volume increases. Otherwise, the market will continue to drift sideways," Haydaroglu said.

Over the week, the index gained 1.8 percent after last week's 4.1 percent loss. Delay in settlements of share transactions because of the holiday had triggered some buying on Tuesday when the index jumped 2.2 percent.
Deals done on Tuesday will be settled on April 24 and those made on Wednesday and today will be settled on April 25.

Of the 247 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 123 to 61 and 63 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial edged 0.26 percent higher to 1,529, the IMKB Services firmed 0.42 percent to 1,432 and the IMKB Financial gained 1.16 percent to 1,655.
Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 200,000 lira and Sevgi hospital SVGSH.IS which closed at 9,900 lira. They made up 12.5 percent of the total turnover.
Shares representing partial capital of Sevgi hospital, the first Turkish health institution to go public, began trading on the national market at an opening price of 9,000 lira today.
